Trajectory input

Priyansh Srivastava

Source: vignettes/trajectory-input.Rmd
trajectory-input.Rmd

Abstract

scMaSigPro needs one pseudotime value and one path label per cell, and nothing else from the tool that inferred the trajectory. This vignette describes that input and builds it from the output of slingshot, from a trajectory graph and from a Monocle3 object.

The input contract

Trajectory inference tools describe a trajectory in different ways: slingshot fits one principal curve per lineage and gives every cell a pseudotime and a weight on each lineage (Street et al. 2018), Monocle3 learns a principal graph and gives every cell one pseudotime from a root node (Cao et al. 2019), and tradeSeq takes such weights to fit its own models (Van den Berge et al. 2020). scMaSigPro needs much less: for every cell,

  • one pseudotime value, a number that orders the cells of a path, and
  • one path label, the path that the cell belongs to.

Every cell has one path label: scMaSigPro uses hard assignments. When the paths of a trajectory share their first cells, as the branches of a tree share its trunk, those cells get labels of their own:

  • the cells on every path get the root label;
  • the cells on some of the paths but not all of them get a link label, the names of those paths joined by a separator, _links_ by default;
  • every other cell gets the name of its path, an end path.

sc.restruct() uses these labels to add the bins of the root and of the links to the end paths that share them; the Shared root vignette shows how.

The two columns enter scMaSigPro in one of two ways:

  • as_scmp() takes a SingleCellExperiment whose colData() holds them;
  • create_scmp() takes a count matrix, genes by cells, and a data frame with one row per cell, named by cell, that holds them.

The rest of this vignette builds this table from the output of trajectory tools. The bundled data set multi.lin.sce serves as the example: a simulated trajectory with three end points (Van den Berge et al. 2020; Saelens et al. 2019), whose cells Monocle3 placed on three paths that share a root and a link.

library(scMaSigPro)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)

data("multi.lin.sce", package = "scMaSigPro")
table(colData(multi.lin.sce)$group)
#> 
#>           path_Y_15           path_Y_18 path_Y_18|path_Y_15           path_Y_52 
#>                 307                 676                  43                 498 
#>                root 
#>                 453

From lineage weights

assign_paths() turns lineage weights into path labels. It takes a matrix of weights, one row per cell and one column per lineage, and the pseudotime of each cell, either as a matrix of the same shape (one pseudotime per lineage, as slingshot gives it) or as one vector (one pseudotime shared by every lineage, as Monocle3 gives it). A cell is on a lineage when its weight there is at least min_weight, 0.5 by default, and its pseudotime there is known.

A small example with three lineages shows the rules:

weights <- rbind(
    cell1 = c(A = 1, B = 1, C = 1),
    cell2 = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.8, C = 0.1),
    cell3 = c(A = 1, B = 0, C = 0),
    cell4 = c(A = 0, B = 0, C = 0.7),
    cell5 = c(A = 0.2, B = 0.3, C = 0.1)
)
pseudotime <- rbind(
    cell1 = c(A = 1, B = 1.2, C = 0.8),
    cell2 = c(A = 4, B = 5, C = NA),
    cell3 = c(A = 9, B = NA, C = NA),
    cell4 = c(A = NA, B = NA, C = 7),
    cell5 = c(A = 2, B = 2, C = 2)
)
assign_paths(pseudotime, weights)
#> 1 of 5 cells are on no lineage (no weight of at least 0.5 with a pseudotime) and are left out.
#>       Pseudotime      Path
#> cell1        1.0      root
#> cell2        4.5 A_links_B
#> cell3        9.0         A
#> cell4        7.0         C

cell1 is on every lineage and becomes a root cell; cell2 is on A and B only and gets the link label A_links_B; cell3 and cell4 are on one lineage each. A cell on several lineages gets the mean of its pseudotimes there. cell5 is on no lineage and is left out, with a message.

The weights are compared with min_weight as they are given. slingshot’s curve weights are close to 1 on every lineage for the cells of the root; for weights that add up to 1 in each cell, a min_weight below 1 divided by the number of lineages keeps the root cells.

From slingshot

slingshot needs a low-dimensional embedding and clusters of cells. Here the embedding is the t-SNE of multi.lin.sce and the clusters are its Monocle3 path labels, with the root as the start and the three end paths as the end clusters. This section runs when slingshot and DelayedMatrixStats, which its lineage inference needs, are installed.

leaves <- c("path_Y_15", "path_Y_18", "path_Y_52")
sds <- slingshot::slingshot(
    reducedDim(multi.lin.sce, "TSNE"),
    clusterLabels = colData(multi.lin.sce)$group,
    start.clus = "root",
    end.clus = leaves
)
slingshot::slingLineages(sds)
#> $Lineage1
#> [1] "root"                "path_Y_18|path_Y_15" "path_Y_15"          
#> 
#> $Lineage2
#> [1] "root"                "path_Y_18|path_Y_15" "path_Y_18"          
#> 
#> $Lineage3
#> [1] "root"      "path_Y_52"

Each lineage ends in one of the end clusters, which gives it its name:

ends <- vapply(
    slingshot::slingLineages(sds), function(l) l[length(l)], character(1)
)
time <- slingshot::slingPseudotime(sds)
weights <- slingshot::slingCurveWeights(sds)
colnames(time) <- colnames(weights) <- ends

cells <- assign_paths(time, weights)
table(cells$Path)
#> 
#>                 path_Y_15 path_Y_15_links_path_Y_18 path_Y_15_links_path_Y_52 
#>                       352                       159                         2 
#>                 path_Y_18 path_Y_18_links_path_Y_52                 path_Y_52 
#>                       720                         3                       545 
#>                      root 
#>                       196

The two tools draw the borders between the root, the link and the end paths in different places; slingshot, for one, puts fewer cells in the root than Monocle3 does here. Soft weights also place a few cells on two lineages that share nothing but the root, here path_Y_52 and one of the other two; their labels look like links, but no segment of the trajectory joins those paths. They are so few that the simplest choice is to leave them out:

link <- "path_Y_15_links_path_Y_18"
cells <- cells[cells$Path %in% c("root", link, leaves), ]
table(
    slingshot = cells$Path,
    monocle3 = colData(multi.lin.sce)[rownames(cells), "group"]
)
#>                            monocle3
#> slingshot                   path_Y_15 path_Y_18 path_Y_18|path_Y_15 path_Y_52
#>   path_Y_15                       297         0                   4         0
#>   path_Y_15_links_path_Y_18         6         0                  18        19
#>   path_Y_18                         4       676                  21        19
#>   path_Y_52                         0         0                   0       460
#>   root                              0         0                   0         0
#>                            monocle3
#> slingshot                   root
#>   path_Y_15                   51
#>   path_Y_15_links_path_Y_18  116
#>   path_Y_18                    0
#>   path_Y_52                   85
#>   root                       196

The cell table goes to create_scmp() with the counts of its cells. The workflow then runs as for any other input; here on the first 100 genes, with the root and the link added to the end paths by sc.restruct():

genes <- rownames(multi.lin.sce)[seq_len(100)]
scmp_ob <- create_scmp(
    counts = counts(multi.lin.sce)[genes, rownames(cells)],
    cell_data = cells,
    ptime_col = "Pseudotime",
    path_col = "Path"
)
scmp_ob <- sc.squeeze(scmp_ob)
scmp_ob <- sc.restruct(scmp_ob,
    end_node_list = as.list(leaves),
    root_node = "root",
    link_node_list = list(link),
    verbose = FALSE
)
plotBinTile(scmp_ob)

scmp_ob <- sc.set.poly(scmp_ob, poly_degree = 2)
scmp_ob <- sc.p.vector(scmp_ob, verbose = FALSE)
scmp_ob <- sc.t.fit(scmp_ob, verbose = FALSE)
scmp_ob <- sc.filter(scmp_ob, rsq = 0.7, vars = "groups")
res <- scmpResults(scmp_ob)
colSums(as.data.frame(res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(res))]))
#> sig_path_Y_18vspath_Y_15 sig_path_Y_52vspath_Y_15            sig_path_Y_15 
#>                       22                       27                       25

From a trajectory graph

Tools that describe a trajectory as a graph, such as the principal graph of Monocle3 or a minimum spanning tree of clusters, give every cell a node of the graph. paths_from_graph() turns the graph into lineage weights: each lineage is the path from the root node to an end node, and a cell has weight 1 on the lineages that pass through its node and 0 elsewhere. It finds the paths with the igraph package (Csárdi and Nepusz 2006).

The graph here has the Monocle3 path labels of multi.lin.sce as its nodes: the root joins the end path path_Y_52 and the link, and the link joins the other two end paths.

edges <- rbind(
    c("root", "path_Y_52"),
    c("root", "path_Y_18|path_Y_15"),
    c("path_Y_18|path_Y_15", "path_Y_15"),
    c("path_Y_18|path_Y_15", "path_Y_18")
)
cell_node <- colData(multi.lin.sce)$group
names(cell_node) <- colnames(multi.lin.sce)
graph_weights <- paths_from_graph(cell_node, edges, root = "root")
head(graph_weights)
#>    path_Y_52 path_Y_15 path_Y_18
#> C2         1         1         1
#> C3         1         1         1
#> C4         0         1         0
#> C5         1         1         1
#> C6         1         0         0
#> C7         1         1         1

The end nodes are the nodes with one edge other than the root, in the order in which they appear in edges; endpoints chooses them. With the Monocle3 pseudotime, shared by every lineage, assign_paths() gives back the path labels of the data set, with the link written in the _links_ format:

graph_cells <- assign_paths(
    colData(multi.lin.sce)$Monocle3_Pseudotime, graph_weights
)
table(graph_cells$Path)
#> 
#>                 path_Y_15 path_Y_15_links_path_Y_18                 path_Y_18 
#>                       307                        43                       676 
#>                 path_Y_52                      root 
#>                       498                       453

From Monocle3

A Monocle3 cell_data_set after learn_graph() and order_cells() holds the same pieces: the principal graph, the nearest node of each cell, the root node and the pseudotime. The code below builds the cell table from them with paths_from_graph() and assign_paths(). It is not run here: monocle3 is distributed on GitHub, not on CRAN or Bioconductor, so scMaSigPro cannot depend on it.

library(monocle3)
# `cds`: a cell_data_set after learn_graph() and order_cells()
graph <- principal_graph(cds)[["UMAP"]]
aux <- principal_graph_aux(cds)[["UMAP"]]

# The nearest node of each cell, as a node name, and the root node
nearest <- aux$pr_graph_cell_proj_closest_vertex
cell_node <- igraph::V(graph)$name[nearest[, 1]]
names(cell_node) <- rownames(nearest)
root <- aux$root_pr_nodes

# One lineage per end node, then the path label of each cell
weights <- paths_from_graph(cell_node, igraph::as_edgelist(graph),
    root = root
)
cells <- assign_paths(pseudotime(cds), weights)

scmp_ob <- create_scmp(
    counts = counts(cds)[, rownames(cells)],
    cell_data = cells,
    ptime_col = "Pseudotime",
    path_col = "Path"
)

The principal graph often has more end nodes than the branches of interest, and a graph learnt on several partitions has parts that the root cannot reach; endpoints names the end nodes of the lineages to analyse, which must be reachable from the root. Cells on none of these lineages, and cells with an infinite pseudotime, are left out.

Other tools

Any tool will do that gives a pseudotime and a lineage for every cell. With lineage weights, as slingshot and tradeSeq give them, assign_paths() makes the labels; with a graph of nodes, paths_from_graph() makes the weights first. With hard labels already, as multi.lin.sce has them, add the two columns to the colData() and call as_scmp(), or pass the table to create_scmp().
